items.claim: ReserveStock is dispatched inside wrapInTransaction() to the Redis transport, which sends at once, so a worker can handle it before the order is committed (find() returns null) or for an order that was rolled back.
IssueRefundHandler refunds without an idempotency key or an already-refunded check; if the flush or the notification after it throws, the retry refunds again.

ReserveStockHandler turns UnknownSkuException (a SKU missing from the warehouse catalogue, a permanent failure) into RecoverableMessageHandlingException, which is retried without limit, ignoring max_retries.

GenerateShippingLabel carries the Shipment entity instead of its id; the handler gets an unmanaged, stale copy, so setLabelUrl() plus flush() never saves the label URL (and the label can be booked again). May be reported at src/MessageHandler/GenerateShippingLabelHandler.php.
No failure_transport is configured, so messages that exhaust their retries (or throw UnrecoverableMessageHandlingException) are removed from the transport and lost.
ExportOrderToErp is dispatched inside the transaction, so it can be handled before commit or after a rollback.
items.why_fine: It is routed to the Doctrine transport on the ORM's default connection, so the send joins the transaction and rolls back with it.

items.claim: SendOrderConfirmation is dispatched before the order is committed.
items.why_fine: It is dispatched after wrapInTransaction() has returned, so after commit.

items.claim: ExportOrderToErpHandler creates the ERP order again when it is retried, redelivered or runs twice.
items.why_fine: It skips orders that already have an ERP reference and upserts by a stable external id.
